McLaren.summary: McLaren has reshaped the side‑pod inlet and engine cover, refined the rear‑suspension fairings and shifted the straight‑line wing flap to smooth the airflow and trim drag. At the same time, a new cooling‑louvre pattern, sharper floor edge and a re‑worked diffuser aim to squeeze out extra down‑force where the car needs it most. Together, these tweaks should give the car a tighter balance and more grip, helping the team fight for every tenth of a second this weekend.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has tweaked the underside of the car – reshaping the floor and diffuser – to give the car a bigger grip bite on the straights and through fast corners, which should translate into more consistent lap times this weekend. The side‑pods have been narrowed and the cooling vents reshaped to improve airflow and keep the power unit at optimal temperatures, while a new mirror and halo fairing smooth the air around the cockpit for a cleaner rear‑end. In short, the package aims to boost down‑force and reliability, giving the drivers a steadier, faster run on the circuit.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams have given the car a full “under‑body” makeover – new floor panels with sharper edges, a tweaked rear diffuser and updated brake‑duct inlets – all aimed at generating more down‑force and cleaner airflow. The rear suspension cover has been rotated to improve tire contact, while the front brake‑duct now channels air more efficiently, helping the car turn into corners with less turbulence. Together, these tweaks should give Williams a boost in grip and stability, making the car faster and more predictable around this weekend’s circuit.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls (RB) have rolled out a brand‑new front wing and upgraded the front‑corner area with a fresh brake duct and a reshaped lip, plus tweaked the shape of the front suspension arms. These changes smooth the airflow over the car’s nose and under‑car, giving the driver a bit more grip and stability through the corners. In short, the tweaks should translate into better handling and a stronger start, which could be the edge RB needs this weekend.

Audi F1 Team.summary: Audi’s F1 car arrives this weekend with a completely re‑shaped front end and a fresh rear package. The new front wing, nose and surrounding fairings smooth the air into the car, while updated front‑suspension covers keep that flow clean, and a revised floor and diffuser add more down‑force where it counts. At the back, a brand‑new rear‑wing assembly and re‑worked suspension covers and brake ducts tighten the airflow and boost stability, giving Audi a clearer aerodynamic advantage right out of the box.

Cadillac.summary: Cadillac’s latest tweaks give the car a cooler‑running brake system, smoother air over the front suspension, and a reshaped diffuser edge that sticks the car to the track a bit tighter. The result? Drivers can brake deeper into corners, keep the front end more stable through turn‑ins, and carry a little extra speed onto the straights—exactly the edge needed for a strong push this weekend.
